the proposed model of point sources in wave-based acoustic simulation is accurate, flexible, and efficient.

we have presented a novel approach for modeling directional sources in wave-based acoustic simulation that is based on a Fourier-based spatial interpolation strategy and that is shown to yield accurate results.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of sources of arbitrary directivities in volumetric wave-based acoustic simulations.
the modeling of sources with arbitrary directivity and position with respect to an arbitrary grid, and the subsequent implementation of these models in a wave-based simulation framework.
the development of a new model of sources for wave-based acoustic simulation, which is based on a spatio-temporal Fourier-based approximation of Dirac distributions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a source located at an arbitrary position with respect to the underlying grid, the proposed model is capable of providing a very good approximation to the exact solution, and the approximation can be improved by increasing the grid resolution and the order of the approximant.

, in the context of wave-based acoustic simulation, a new model for point sources has been presented, which is based on a Fourier-based approximation of the spatial derivatives of Dirac distributions.

the new method is capable of producing accurate approximations to directional sources of arbitrary directivities, and is therefore a useful addition to the toolbox of wave-based acoustic modeling techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model is capable of accurately modeling sources of arbitrary directivities and locations with respect to a spatial grid.
we provide a new framework for modeling sources in wave-based simulation.
we have developed a new method for modeling point sources with arbitrary directivity in wave-based acoustic simulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and efficient approximation of a source's spatial Fourier transform is sufficient to yield a good approximation of the source itself in the time domain, even when it is highly directional.
, for sources that are not isotropic, a nonseparable approximant is necessary to achieve a reasonable level of accuracy.
the directional source problem can be formulated and solved directly, without the need for intermediate steps in the frequency domain.
